findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh instance, so logs are not recorded
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger(), a brand-new instance, rather than the receiver. All other TestLogger methods record calls into f.DebugLogs/InfoLogs/etc., which tests then assert on. With this change, LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so any test that constructs a TestLogger, passes it to NewLoggerMiddleware, and then inspects InfoLogs will always see zero calls and an empty message — the log entry is recorded on a throwaway logger. The fake should return the receiver itself (f) so recorded logs remain observable, matching how a contextual logger is expected to behave.

findings.title: traceID is no longer included in the "Plugin Request Completed" log entry
findings.body: Before this change, LoggerMiddleware.logRequest explicitly appended "traceID" (from tracing.TraceIDFromContext) to the log params, along with pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName and dsUID. Now those fields are only present if the incoming context carries the contextual attributes added by ContextualLoggerMiddleware — but that middleware never adds a traceID, and the tracing import was removed from this file. Unless pkg/infra/log's ConcreteLogger.FromContext injects traceID automatically (which the old explicit code suggests it does not), the traceID field silently disappears from the egress log line, breaking log-to-trace correlation for anyone relying on the traceID field of this event.

findings.title: Contextual log fields now silently depend on middleware ordering
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware no longer sets pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, or uname itself; it relies on ContextualLoggerMiddleware having already enriched the context via FromContext(ctx). In pluginsintegration.go the ordering is correct (ContextualLoggerMiddleware before LoggerMiddleware), but nothing in the code enforces or documents this dependency — if the LoggerMiddleware is ever used without the ContextualLoggerMiddleware ahead of it (or the order is swapped), the "Plugin Request Completed" log will silently lose all plugin-identifying fields. A comment on logRequest or NewLoggerMiddleware documenting this requirement would prevent a subtle observability regression.
